By Farhan Rahman

More Teams,
Less Drama

How the 48-team World Cup took the risk out of the group stage

Qatar 2022: Germany won its last group game and still went home. Under the old format, one bad result could end your World Cup.Source: “Germany Crash Out” (Al Jazeera)

The 48-team format made the group stage less exciting: more teams advance, losing is no longer fatal, and more teams’ fates are decided early.

Press → to begin · F for full screen

New to soccer? Start here

How the World Cup group stage works

  1. Teams are split into groups of 4.
  2. Each team plays the other three once. A win is 3 points, a draw is 1. The last round of these games is called the final matchday.
  3. The best teams move on to the knockout rounds. Everyone else goes home.

Think of it like the NFL: imagine if two out of every three teams made the playoffs. The regular season would matter a lot less.

8 groups. Only the top 2 in each group advance: 16 of 32 teams.

✓ top 2 advance✓ third place also advances✕ goes home

These are the real 2026 results: third place advanced in 8 of the 12 groups.

Sources: “What Is the Format” (FIFA); Outlook Sports Desk (Outlook India)

Case study · The incentive problem

Austria vs. Algeria: a draw suited both

  1. KickoffBoth teams know a draw sends them both through.
  2. Late, 2–2Algeria starts playing keep-away. The crowd whistles.
  3. Final minutesAlgeria scores to lead 3–2. In stoppage time (added time at the end), Austria ties it on the last play: 3–3.
  4. ResultBoth advance. Iran, not even on the field, is eliminated.
Step 1 of 4
Source: Skretta (AP, via TSN)

Flashback, 1982Austria and West Germany seemed to stop playing once 1–0 sent both through, knocking out Algeria. The new format recreated the same setup. In 2026, the game only came alive once Algeria’s late goal put Austria at risk.Source: Skretta (AP, via TSN)

The other side

“But there were more goals!”

Group-stage goals per game

2.54
2.50

201820222026
Source: St. Martin (Northeastern Global News)
Concede itThe 2026 group stage had the most goals per game since 1958, and 99.7% of seats were filled.Sources: St. Martin (Northeastern Global News); “Records Tumble” (FIFA)
Rebut itNortheastern’s analysis linked part of the jump to having more teams, which added more games between strong and weak teams. Canada 6–0 Qatar was a mismatch, not a thriller. Full stadiums show demand for the World Cup, not tension in each game. More goals is not the same as more at stake.Sources: St. Martin (Northeastern Global News); Ozkan (Anadolu Agency)

The bottom line

Excitement comesfrom risk,not goals.

Next World Cup, watch the final matchday and count how many games still matter. Then ask yourself: should FIFA keep this format for 2030?
